However, that system was soon crippled by state priorities, the overemphasis on "labor quantity", administrative requirements, target production quotas and the use of inefficient labor models.

These issues were the result of a blend of limited technological capacity and path-dependency in the Great Leap project, in which the state became involved in forcing rural areas to adopt inefficient methods because of inadequate investment in mature technology and institutions. The Great Leap Forward was a major economic and social campaign launched in 1958 by the Chinese Communist Party. The official death toll is estimated to be between 15 million and 45 million people.
